summary:
Root fs (`/dev/vda` ext4) is persistent; `/opt` and `/var/lib` will survive reboot. The unit is already enabled and points to `/opt/builder/app.py`. Let me create the app.Now verify behavior with curl.Service works including binary/empty bodies. Now verify records survive a service restart.The service is deployed and durable. Summary:

**Implementation** — `/opt/builder/app.py`: stdlib-only `ThreadingHTTPServer` on port 8080.
- `GET /health` → `200` body `ready`
- `PUT /records/<id>` → stores raw body bytes (atomic `tempfile` + `os.replace` + `fsync` of file and dir) → `204`
- `GET /records/<id>` → returns exact stored bytes → `200`
- IDs restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`; binary-safe; empty bodies supported.

**Durability** — records stored at `/var/lib/builder-app/records/` on the persistent ext4 root (`/dev/vda`). Verified records (including binary `hello\0world\n{"k":1}` and an empty body) survive a `systemctl restart`.

**Boot autonomy** — `builder-app.service` is `enabled` (WantedBy=multi-user.target) with `Restart=always`. The app file lives on persistent root fs, so after reboot systemd starts it without agent help and existing records persist.

The unit went from `failed (start-limit-hit)` to `active (running)`, reset via `systemctl reset-failed` then `restart`.
